title: Pan-seared ribeye with butter baste
desc: Dry steak, very hot pan, flip every minute, butter-baste, thermometer, rest. Then make a pan sauce in the same pan.
reheat: Slice cold for salad rather than reheating.
left: Cold sliced steak on a salad with chimichurri.
trouble: Steak was wet or pan not hot enough — pat dry, wait for the oil to shimmer.
Use the thermometer, pull at 52 °C for medium-rare (it rises while resting).
Use sunflower oil, not butter, for the sear; add butter only at the end.
goes: Peppercorn sauce, chimichurri, green beans, mushrooms.
ing: 3 cm thick, out of the fridge 30 min

steps.t: Take the steaks out 30 minutes early. Pat them completely dry with kitchen paper and salt both sides generously.
steps.w: A dry surface browns; a wet one steams. Room-temperature meat cooks more evenly.
steps.m: Cooking straight from the fridge with a wet surface.
steps.img: two raw ribeye steaks being patted dry and salted on a board

steps.t: Heat a cast-iron or heavy pan on high for 3–4 minutes. Add the oil; it should shimmer and just begin to smoke.
steps.w: A very hot heavy pan keeps its heat when the cold steak goes in.
steps.c: Oil shimmers, first wisp of smoke.
steps.m: Not hot enough — no crust.
steps.img: oil shimmering in a very hot cast iron pan

steps.t: Lay the steaks in, away from you. Turn them every minute with tongs for about 6–8 minutes in total.
steps.w: Frequent flipping cooks evenly from both sides and still builds a crust.
steps.c: Deep brown crust on both sides.
steps.m: Pressing the steak down — juices run out.
steps.img: ribeye steaks searing in a cast iron pan with deep brown crust

steps.t: Lower to medium, add the butter, garlic and thyme. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 1–2 minutes until the thermometer reads 52 °C in the centre (medium-rare).
steps.w: Basting adds flavour and cooks the top gently; the thermometer removes the guessing.
steps.c: Butter foaming nut-brown; 52 °C in the thickest part.
steps.m: Butter in at the start on high heat — it burns.
steps.img: spooning foaming butter with garlic and thyme over steak in a pan

steps.t: Rest the steaks 5 minutes on a board, loosely covered. Meanwhile make a pan sauce in the same pan. Slice against the grain.
steps.w: Resting lets juices settle; the temperature rises to about 55 °C.
steps.c: Pink and juicy inside, little juice on the board.
steps.m: Cutting straight away — juice floods the board.
steps.img: sliced medium-rare ribeye steak on a wooden board

title: Lemon-garlic roast chicken
desc: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and thyme, crisp skin, juicy meat — then gravy from the tray and stock from the bones.
reheat: Covered, 180 °C until piping hot, or eat cold.
left: Chicken salad, avgolemono soup, and make stock from the carcass.
trouble: Dry the skin well and roast at 200 °C fan for the first 20 minutes.
Pull it at 74 °C in the thigh and rest it — don't go by time alone.
Back in the oven until the thigh reads 74 °C.
goes: Gravy, roast potatoes, green beans, Greek salad.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C fan. Pat the chicken dry inside and out. Do not wash it (washing spreads bacteria round the sink).
steps.w: Dry skin crisps; rinsing raw chicken splashes germs.
steps.m: Washing the chicken under the tap.
steps.img: whole raw chicken patted dry with paper towels on a tray

steps.t: Mix the soft butter with lemon zest, chopped thyme leaves, salt and pepper. Rub it over and under the breast skin.
steps.w: Butter under the skin bastes the breast as it roasts.
steps.m: Tearing the skin — slide fingers gently.
steps.img: hands rubbing herb butter under the skin of a raw chicken

steps.t: Put the lemon halves, garlic and remaining thyme inside the bird. Sit it on the onion slices in the tray, drizzle with oil.
steps.w: Onions lift the bird and flavour the juices for gravy.
steps.c: Bird sitting on an onion bed.
steps.m: Forgetting the onion — juices burn on the tray.
steps.img: chicken stuffed with lemon and garlic sitting on sliced onions in a roasting tray

steps.t: Roast about 1 hour 15 minutes (45 min per kg + 20 min) until the thickest part of the thigh reads 74 °C and the juices run clear.
steps.w: 74 °C is the safe temperature for poultry.
steps.c: Golden crisp skin; 74 °C in the thigh.
steps.m: Going by time only — ovens differ.
steps.img: golden roast chicken in the oven with a thermometer in the thigh

steps.t: Rest 15 minutes, loosely covered with foil. Make gravy from the tray meanwhile.
steps.w: Resting keeps the breast juicy.
steps.m: Covering tightly — the skin softens.
steps.img: roast chicken resting on a board loosely covered with foil

steps.t: Carve: legs off first, then the breast in slices. Keep the carcass for stock.
steps.w: The bones make free stock.
steps.c: Neat pieces, carcass in the fridge.
steps.m: Throwing the bones away.
steps.img: carving a roast chicken on a board

title: Spaghetti carbonara (Roman, no cream)
desc: Guanciale or pancetta, egg yolks, pecorino, black pepper and pasta water — the sauce is made by the heat of the pasta, off the hob.
reheat: Doesn't reheat well — eat at once.
trouble: Pan was on the heat — mix the eggs in off the heat with pasta water.
Loosen with more hot pasta water and toss.
Pasta water too salty — salt it less than usual; the cheese and pork are salty.

steps.t: Boil 2 litres of water with only 12 g salt — less than usual. Cook the spaghetti 1 minute under the packet time.
steps.w: Pecorino and guanciale bring a lot of salt.
steps.m: Sea-salty water — the finished dish gets too salty.
steps.img: spaghetti boiling in a large pot

steps.t: Mix the eggs, most of the pecorino and lots of pepper into a paste in a bowl.
steps.w: A thick paste melts into sauce without lumps.
steps.m: Watery whisked eggs — they scramble more easily.
steps.img: egg yolks grated pecorino and black pepper mixed into a paste in a bowl

steps.t: Cook the guanciale in a cold pan, turning the heat to medium, 6–8 minutes until the fat runs and the edges crisp. Turn off the heat.
steps.w: Starting cold renders the fat slowly; that fat is part of the sauce.
steps.c: Golden and crisp at the edges, fat clear.
steps.m: Burning it on high heat.
steps.img: strips of guanciale rendering in a pan, golden

steps.t: Lift the pasta into the pan with tongs, toss in the fat. Wait 30 seconds off the heat, then add the egg paste and 4–5 tbsp pasta water, tossing hard.
steps.w: Below about 70 °C the egg thickens into a cream; higher it scrambles.
steps.c: Glossy, creamy sauce coating every strand.
steps.m: Doing this on the flame — scrambled eggs.
steps.img: tossing spaghetti with egg and cheese into a glossy carbonara sauce

steps.t: Serve at once with the remaining pecorino and more pepper.
steps.w: The sauce tightens as it cools.
steps.m: Letting it sit.
steps.img: plate of spaghetti carbonara with black pepper and pecorino

title: Ragù bolognese
desc: Soffritto, browned mince, tomato, stock and a little milk, simmered 2 hours. Alcohol-free (no wine).
left: Lasagne, stuffed peppers, freeze in portions.
variant: The other portion: on roast cauliflower or cauliflower rice instead of tagliatelle. Milk can be replaced with cream.
trouble: Brown it in batches in a hot pan.
Simmer longer; stir in a knob of butter.

steps.t: Cook the onion, carrot and celery — the soffritto — in the oil and butter on medium-low for 10 minutes.
steps.w: A slow soffritto is the sweet base of the ragù.
steps.m: Big chunks — dice them small so they melt in.
steps.img: finely diced onion carrot and celery softening in a heavy pan

steps.t: Push the vegetables to the side, turn the heat to high and add the mince in two batches; break it up and let it brown well before stirring.
steps.w: Browning creates savoury flavour; a crowded pan stews the meat grey.
steps.c: Brown crumbly mince, pan sizzling not bubbling.
steps.m: All the mince at once — grey and watery.
steps.img: beef mince browning in a heavy pan with vegetables pushed aside

steps.t: Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then the passata, stock, bay, salt and pepper.
steps.w: Frying the paste deepens the colour and taste.
steps.m: Skipping the paste fry.
steps.img: tomato and stock added to browned mince

steps.t: Simmer on the lowest heat, lid ajar, 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes. Add the milk and nutmeg for the last 30 minutes.
steps.w: Long simmering makes the meat tender and the sauce deep; milk softens the acidity (the Bologna way).
steps.c: Thick, glossy, fat shining on top; a spoon leaves a trail.
steps.m: Boiling hard — tough meat, sauce catches.
steps.img: thick ragu bolognese simmering in a heavy pan

steps.t: Cook the tagliatelle, toss with some ragù and a splash of pasta water; serve the on roast cauliflower. Parmesan on top.
steps.w: Tossing pasta with the sauce makes it cling.
steps.m: Sauce dumped on top of plain pasta.
steps.img: tagliatelle tossed with ragu bolognese topped with parmesan

title: Crispy-skin salmon
desc: Skin-side down in a hot pan, pressed flat for 10 seconds, left alone until the skin is glass-crisp.
reheat: Eat cold flaked into a salad.
trouble: Pan not hot enough or moved too early — it releases when crisp.
Press the fillet flat with a fish slice for the first 10–15 seconds.
Pull it at 50–52 °C centre; it finishes off the heat.
goes: Beurre blanc, salsa verde, green beans, cauliflower rice.

steps.t: Pat the salmon skin very dry with paper, scrape it with the back of a knife, salt the skin.
steps.w: Moisture is the enemy of crispy skin.
steps.m: Salting an hour early — draws water out to the surface.
steps.img: salmon fillets skin up being patted dry with paper towel

steps.t: Heat the oil in a pan on medium-high. Lay the fillets skin-side down and press them flat with a fish slice for 15 seconds.
steps.w: Skin contracts in the heat and curls; pressing keeps full contact.
steps.m: Cold pan — the skin sticks and tears.
steps.img: salmon fillet pressed skin-side down in a hot pan with a fish slice

steps.t: Leave it alone 5–6 minutes on medium, until the flesh has turned opaque three-quarters of the way up the side.
steps.w: Most of the cooking happens through the skin, which protects the flesh.
steps.c: Opaque line creeping up the side; skin releases easily.
steps.m: Moving it around.
steps.img: side view of salmon cooking, opaque colour rising up the fillet

steps.t: Flip, add the butter, cook 30–60 seconds. Serve skin up with lemon.
steps.w: A brief kiss on the flesh side keeps the centre moist.
steps.m: Serving skin-down — it steams soft.
steps.img: crispy skin salmon fillet skin side up with a lemon wedge

title: Chicken curry from scratch
desc: Curry base, browned chicken thighs and cream — no coconut, no yogurt.
variant: Make a second small pan with cauliflower and chickpeas in the base instead of chicken.
trouble: Fry the spices longer in oil.

steps.t: Make the curry base: onions in 2 tbsp oil 15–20 minutes until golden, then garlic and ginger 2 minutes, spices 1 minute, tomatoes 10 minutes.
steps.w: The base is where the flavour is built.
steps.c: Thick, deep orange, oil at the edges.
steps.m: Rushing the onions.
steps.img: thick orange curry base simmering in a pan

steps.t: In another pan, brown the salted chicken in 1 tbsp oil on high, in batches, 4 minutes.
steps.w: Browned edges add roasted flavour.
steps.c: Golden edges; not cooked through yet.
steps.m: Overcrowding — boiled, pale chicken.
steps.img: chicken thigh chunks browning in a hot pan

steps.t: Add the chicken to the base with a splash of water and simmer 15 minutes until 74 °C inside.
steps.w: Thighs stay juicy in a simmer.
steps.m: Hard boiling — stringy chicken.
steps.img: chicken curry simmering

steps.t: Pour in the cream and let it bubble gently for 2 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon. Taste, salt, scatter coriander.
steps.w: Yogurt curdles if it boils — off the heat it stays creamy.
steps.m: Adding yogurt on full heat.
steps.img: creamy chicken curry garnished with fresh coriander

title: Mushroom risotto
desc: Toasted rice, hot stock added a ladle at a time, stirring, then butter and parmesan. Vegetarian with vegetable stock.
reheat: Leftovers: arancini or a crispy rice cake in a pan.
left: Fry into crispy cakes the next day (within 24 h).
variant: Small portion only — it's a learning recipe, high in carbs.
trouble: Overcooked or stirred too hard at the end — stop when the grain has a little bite.
Season the stock, more parmesan, a squeeze of lemon.

steps.t: Soak the porcini in 150 ml hot water for 10 minutes. Chop them; add the soaking water (leave grit at the bottom) to the hot stock and keep it simmering.
steps.w: Porcini water is intensely flavoured; hot stock keeps the rice cooking steadily.
steps.m: Adding cold stock — it stops the cooking each time.
steps.img: dried porcini soaking in hot water next to simmering stock

steps.t: Brown the fresh mushrooms in the oil on high; set aside.
steps.w: Browned mushrooms taste deeper than stewed ones.
steps.m: Crowding.
steps.img: mushrooms browning in a pan

steps.t: Melt half the butter, soften the shallot 3 minutes, add garlic, then the rice. Stir 2 minutes until the grains look glassy at the edges.
steps.w: Toasting coats each grain in fat so it releases starch slowly.
steps.c: Grains translucent at the edges, white centre, slight crackle.
steps.m: Rinsing the rice — the surface starch makes the creaminess.
steps.img: arborio rice toasting with shallots, grains translucent at the edges

steps.t: Add one ladle of hot stock and stir until almost absorbed; repeat for 18–20 minutes. Add the porcini and browned mushrooms halfway.
steps.w: Stirring rubs starch off the grains, which thickens the liquid into a creamy sauce.
steps.c: Grains soft with a slight bite; texture loose and wavy.
steps.m: Adding all the stock at once.
steps.img: ladle of stock poured into risotto while stirring

steps.t: Off the heat, beat in the rest of the butter and the parmesan; cover 2 minutes, season, serve on warm plates.
steps.w: Beating in fat and cheese (mantecatura) makes it glossy.
steps.c: Flows slowly when the plate is tilted.
steps.m: Stiff risotto — add a splash more stock.
steps.img: creamy mushroom risotto spreading on a plate with parmesan

title: Roasted Mediterranean vegetables & cauliflower rice
desc: High heat, room on the tray, oil and salt — vegetables that taste roasted, plus 5-minute cauliflower rice.
reheat: Hot oven or air fryer 5 minutes.
left: Blend leftover veg into soup; add to omelettes.
trouble: Tray too full — use two trays; oven at least 200 °C.
Don't cover it; fry in a hot pan so steam escapes.
goes: Grilled meat, fish, halloumi, yogurt sauce.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 210 °C fan. Halve the mushrooms, cut the broccoli into florets, cut the pepper and red onion into similar chunks.
steps.w: Same size = done at the same time.
steps.m: Tiny pieces burn, giant ones stay raw.
steps.img: chopped mediterranean vegetables on a board

steps.t: Toss with the oil, oregano and salt, spread on one or two trays with space between pieces. Roast 25–30 minutes, turning once.
steps.w: Space lets moisture escape so vegetables brown; crowding steams them.
steps.c: Edges caramelised and dark, soft inside.
steps.m: Piling them up on one tray.
steps.img: roasted vegetables with caramelised edges on a tray

steps.t: Cauliflower rice: pulse the florets in the food processor until rice-sized (or grate them).
steps.w: Small even pieces cook in minutes.
steps.m: Over-processing to mush.
steps.img: cauliflower pulsed into rice-sized pieces in a food processor

steps.t: Fry the cauliflower rice in a hot pan with a little oil and salt for 4–5 minutes, uncovered. Stir in parsley.
steps.w: Uncovered, the steam escapes and it stays fluffy.
steps.c: Tender with a slight bite, lightly golden.
steps.m: Lid on — soggy.
steps.img: cauliflower rice frying in a pan with parsley

title: Greek salad (horiatiki)
desc: Ripe tomatoes, onion, pepper, olives, capers, a slab of feta, oregano and good olive oil.
trouble: Salt only at the table; drain very juicy tomatoes.

steps.t: Cut the tomatoes into chunky wedges, the onion and pepper into thin rings.
steps.w: Chunky tomatoes hold their juice.
steps.m: Dicing small — it turns watery.
steps.img: tomato wedges red onion rings and pepper rings on a board

steps.t: Arrange in a bowl with the olives and capers. Put the feta slab on top, sprinkle with oregano.
steps.w: A whole slab is traditional — everyone breaks off their own.
steps.c: Pretty pile with white feta on top.
steps.m: Crumbling the feta into dust.
steps.img: greek village salad with a slab of feta and oregano

steps.t: Pour over the olive oil and vinegar, add a pinch of salt just before eating.
steps.w: Salt draws out tomato juice that mixes with the oil — the best part.
steps.m: Salting early.
steps.img: olive oil being poured over a horiatiki salad

title: Slow-baked lamb parcels with potatoes
desc: The slow-roasted lamb sealed in parchment with potatoes, lemon, garlic, oregano and cinnamon until it falls off the bone. No wine.
reheat: Covered in the oven at 170 °C until piping hot.
left: Shred into a salad; lamb and potato hash.
variant: Slow cooker: potatoes at the bottom, lamb on top, marinade over, LOW 8 h; then 20 min in a hot oven to brown. roast extra potatoes, peppers and halloumi in a separate parcel.
trouble: Not long enough — another 30–60 minutes sealed.
Parcel leaked — seal tightly with foil over the paper.

steps.t: Rub the lamb with lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper. Marinate 1 hour or overnight in the fridge.
steps.w: Salt and acid season the meat deeply.
steps.m: Skipping the salt — bland lamb.
steps.img: lamb shoulder pieces rubbed with lemon olive oil and oregano

steps.t: Heat the oven to 160 °C fan. Lay two large sheets of baking paper over foil in the tray. Put the potatoes, onion, garlic, cinnamon and bay in the middle, lamb on top, pour over the marinade.
steps.w: The parcel traps steam — the meat braises in its own juices.
steps.m: Too small a sheet — it can't be sealed.
steps.img: lamb on potatoes in the centre of baking paper in a roasting tray

steps.t: Fold and scrunch the paper and foil into a tightly sealed parcel. Roast 3½ hours.
steps.w: Low heat, sealed, melts the collagen in the shoulder into gelatine.
steps.c: Smells amazing after 2 hours; parcel puffed.
steps.m: Opening it to check — steam escapes.
steps.img: sealed parchment and foil parcel in a roasting tray

steps.t: Open the parcel, turn the oven to 200 °C and roast 20–30 minutes more to brown the top.
steps.w: Browning adds colour and crispy edges.
steps.c: Lamb falls off the bone; potatoes golden.
steps.m: Leaving it sealed — pale.
steps.img: opened foil parcel with golden falling-apart lamb and potatoes

title: Moussaka (yogurt topping)
desc: Roasted aubergine and potato layers, spiced beef sauce, and a baked yogurt-egg-parmesan topping instead of a milk béchamel.
variant: Classic version uses béchamel — swap the topping for the béchamel lesson.
trouble: Roast with a brush of oil instead of frying.
Simmer the meat sauce until thick; rest the moussaka 20 minutes before cutting.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C fan. Brush the aubergine and potato slices with oil, salt them, roast on trays 20–25 minutes until soft and golden.
steps.w: Roasting uses far less oil than frying and gives the same softness.
steps.m: Frying aubergine — it drinks the oil.
steps.img: roasted aubergine and potato slices on trays

steps.t: Meanwhile soften the onion and garlic, brown the mince, add paste, tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, bay, salt. Simmer 25 minutes until thick.
steps.w: A thick sauce keeps the layers from going soupy.
steps.c: Thick, spoon leaves a clear trail.
steps.m: Watery sauce.
steps.img: thick spiced beef tomato sauce in a pan

steps.t: Whisk the yogurt, eggs, half the parmesan and nutmeg.
steps.w: Eggs set the yogurt into a custardy topping when baked.
steps.m: Using thin yogurt — use strained Greek.
steps.img: yogurt egg and parmesan whisked in a bowl

steps.t: Layer in the dish: potatoes, half the aubergine, all the meat, the rest of the aubergine; spread the topping, sprinkle remaining parmesan. Bake at 180 °C fan 40–45 minutes.
steps.w: Potatoes on the bottom soak up juices and support the slices.
steps.m: Cutting it hot — rest 20 minutes first.
steps.img: golden baked moussaka in an oven dish

steps.t: Rest 20 minutes before cutting into squares.
steps.w: Layers set as it cools slightly.
steps.m: Cutting straight away — it slumps.
steps.img: a square slice of moussaka showing layers

title: Pork braised with coriander seed (alcohol-free)
desc: Pork braised with crushed coriander seeds. Often made with red wine — this version uses stock and red wine vinegar for the same tang, zero alcohol.
left: The lunch the next day with yogurt-dill sauce and a salad.
variant: Slow cooker: brown the pork, then everything in the slow cooker on LOW 6–7 h; reduce the sauce in a pan at the end. The classic version uses 300 ml dry red wine instead of stock + vinegar.
trouble: Simmer longer, lid on, low heat.

steps.t: Crush the coriander seeds coarsely in a mortar. Marinate the pork with half the seeds, the vinegar, stock and pepper for at least 2 hours (or overnight) in the fridge.
steps.w: Coriander is the signature of this braise; the acid tenderises and flavours.
steps.m: Using ground coriander — less aroma.
steps.img: pork cubes marinating with crushed coriander seeds

steps.t: Lift the pork out and pat dry (keep the marinade). Brown it in the oil in batches on high.
steps.w: Dry meat browns; browning makes the sauce taste of something.
steps.m: Tipping in the wet pork with marinade — it boils.
steps.img: pork cubes browning in batches in a heavy pan

steps.t: Return all the pork, pour in the marinade, add the remaining coriander, bay, cinnamon and salt. Cover and simmer gently 1 hour.
steps.w: Slow simmering makes the shoulder tender.
steps.m: Boiling hard.
steps.img: pork braise simmering in a covered pan

steps.t: Uncover and reduce 10–15 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the meat.
steps.w: Reduction concentrates the coriander-vinegar sauce.
steps.m: Serving it soupy.
steps.img: glossy dark pork braise with coriander seeds in a pan

title: Oven sea bass, Greek style
desc: Whole sea bass baked on tomatoes, onion and lemon with oregano and olive oil, finished with ladolemono.
trouble: Pull it when the flesh flakes at the backbone; ~20 min for 450 g.
Lay it on the vegetables or baking paper.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C fan. Spread the tomatoes, onion and garlic in a tray, with half the oil, salt and oregano.
steps.w: A vegetable bed keeps the fish moist and makes the sauce.
steps.m: Fish straight on bare metal — sticks.
steps.img: cherry tomatoes onions and garlic in a roasting tray

steps.t: Make 3 slashes on each side of the fish. Salt inside and out, stuff with lemon slices and parsley. Lay on the vegetables, drizzle with oil.
steps.w: Slashes let the heat in evenly.
steps.m: Deep slashes to the bone in thin fish — they fall apart.
steps.img: whole sea bass with slashes stuffed with lemon and parsley on tomatoes

steps.t: Bake 18–22 minutes until the flesh at the thickest part is opaque and flakes from the bone (60 °C).
steps.w: Whole fish on the bone stays juicy.
steps.m: Overbaking — dry fish.
steps.img: baked whole sea bass on roasted tomatoes

steps.t: Spoon the lemon juice and tray juices over and serve.
steps.w: Fresh acid at the end brightens fish.
steps.m: Forgetting the juices.
steps.img: sea bass served with lemon juice and tray juices

title: Christmas dinner: turkey crown, roast potatoes, carrots, sprouts, stuffing & gravy
desc: The full dinner for 4–6 with an oven timeline: brined-butter turkey crown, crisp potatoes, roast carrots and sprouts, sage stuffing, gravy.
reheat: Turkey: covered with gravy, 170 °C until piping hot.
left: Turkey salad, turkey curry, stock from the bones.
variant: A halloumi-and-veg traybake shares the oven; the stuffing is vegetarian if made with vegetable stock.
trouble: Thermometer: pull at 72 °C in the breast and rest 30 min (rises to 74).
Parboil, rough up, very hot fat, one layer, don't crowd.
Follow the timeline; the turkey rests 30–40 min while the oven goes up for potatoes.

steps.t: Timeline (dinner at 18:00): 14:30 oven 180 °C fan. Mix the butter, thyme, lemon zest, garlic, salt and pepper; push it under the turkey skin and over the top.
steps.w: Butter under the skin keeps the breast moist.
steps.m: Turkey straight from the fridge — cooks unevenly.
steps.img: herb butter being pushed under the skin of a turkey crown

steps.t: 15:00 roast the turkey ~40 minutes per kg (about 1 h 40 min for 2.5 kg) until the breast reads 72 °C. Baste every 30 minutes.
steps.w: Pulling at 72 °C and resting carries it to 74 °C without drying.
steps.c: Golden skin; 72 °C at the thickest part.
steps.m: Roasting until it 'looks done' — dry turkey.
steps.img: golden roast turkey crown in the oven

steps.t: Meanwhile (15:30): stuffing — soften the onion in 1 tbsp olive oil, mix with breadcrumbs, sage, the egg, vegetable stock and salt; press into a small dish.
steps.w: Baking stuffing separately cooks it safely and keeps it vegetarian.
steps.m: Too dry — add a splash more stock.
steps.img: sage and onion stuffing pressed into a small baking dish

steps.t: 16:00 parboil the potatoes in salted water 8 minutes, drain, shake in the colander to rough the edges. Put the sunflower oil in a tray in the oven to heat.
steps.w: Roughed-up edges become the crunchy bits.
steps.m: Smooth potatoes — less crunch.
steps.img: parboiled potatoes with roughed up fluffy edges in a colander

steps.t: 16:40 turkey out to rest under foil (30–40 min). Oven to 210 °C. Potatoes into the sizzling oil, carrots and sprouts tossed in olive oil and salt on another tray; stuffing in too. Roast 45 minutes, turning potatoes once.
steps.w: Resting the turkey frees the oven for high-heat sides.
steps.c: Potatoes deep golden and crisp, sprouts browned.
steps.m: Opening the oven constantly — it loses heat.
steps.img: crispy roast potatoes carrots and brussels sprouts on trays

steps.t: 17:30 gravy: spoon off the turkey-tray fat, whisk the flour into the juices over medium heat, then the chicken stock; simmer 5 minutes, add resting juices, sieve.
steps.w: Pan juices carry the roast flavour into the gravy.
steps.m: Lumps — whisk and sieve.
steps.img: gravy whisked in a roasting tray

steps.t: 17:50 carve the turkey across the grain and serve everything hot.
steps.w: Carving across the grain gives tender slices.
steps.m: Carving too early — juices run.
steps.img: carved turkey with roast potatoes carrots sprouts stuffing and gravy on a festive table

title: Homemade chicken stock (pot or slow cooker)
desc: Roast-chicken bones + vegetables + water = stock for a month of sauces. Freeze in portions and ice-cube trays.
reheat: Bring to the boil before using.
left: Freeze in 500 ml tubs and ice-cube trays.
variant: Slow cooker: same ingredients, LOW 8–10 hours.
trouble: It boiled — keep it at a lazy simmer; it still tastes fine.
Simmer longer or reduce after straining.

steps.t: Put the carcass, onion, carrot, celery, bay, peppercorns and parsley stalks in a big pot and cover with cold water.
steps.w: Starting cold extracts flavour and gelatine slowly and keeps it clear.
steps.m: Adding salt — season the dish later, not the stock.
steps.img: chicken carcass vegetables and herbs in a large pot covered with water

steps.t: Bring slowly to a simmer, skim off the grey foam, then keep at the barest simmer 2½–3 hours.
steps.w: Hard boiling emulsifies fat into the stock and clouds it.
steps.c: Occasional lazy bubble, liquid turning golden.
steps.m: A rolling boil.
steps.img: grey foam skimmed from simmering stock with a ladle

steps.t: Strain through a sieve. Cool fast: stand the pot in a sink of cold water, then refrigerate; lift off the fat once set.
steps.w: Fast cooling keeps it out of the bacterial danger zone.
steps.c: Golden stock, may wobble like jelly when cold (that's gelatine — good).
steps.m: Leaving it on the hob overnight.
steps.img: golden stock strained into a bowl set in a sink of cold water

steps.t: Portion into labelled 500 ml tubs and an ice-cube tray; freeze. Fridge 3–4 days, freezer 2–3 months.
steps.w: Small portions thaw fast; cubes are perfect for pan sauces.
steps.m: One giant block.
steps.img: stock in labelled tubs and an ice cube tray ready for the freezer

title: Homemade vegetable stock
desc: 45 minutes, cheap vegetables and herb stalks. Vegetarian base for risotto, soups and the other portion.
reheat: Bring to the boil before using.
trouble: Too many brassica scraps (cabbage, broccoli) — leave those out.
More mushrooms or a parmesan rind; reduce after straining.

steps.t: Sweat the onion, carrot, celery, mushrooms and garlic in the oil 8 minutes.
steps.w: A short sweat deepens the flavour.
steps.m: Browning hard — bitter.
steps.img: vegetables sweating in a stock pot

steps.t: Add water, parsley stalks, bay and peppercorns; simmer 40 minutes.
steps.w: Vegetables give up their flavour in under an hour.
steps.m: Simmering for hours — stewed taste.
steps.img: vegetable stock simmering

steps.t: Strain, cool quickly, portion and freeze.
steps.w: Ready-made bases make weeknight cooking fast.
steps.m: Not labelling.
steps.img: vegetable stock strained into jars
